thread:
anil: quick Q — we're seeing intermittent 502s during cert rotations behind an NLB + Gateway API setup. setup: gateway-api (v0.6), tls passthrough, secret-binding to aws cert, service type NodePort. rotation works but some traffic hits fallback cert and returns 502s. anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:

kate: first guess: client IP / session stickiness. are you using externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster? with NLB that can break healthcheck routing. try externalTrafficPolicy: Local for NodePort svc so source IP preserved. also check target-type annotation.

anil: it's currently externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster. streaming endpoints mostly affected (long lived). we do target-type: ip on the svc annotation.

riley: TLS passthrough means the NLB doesn't terminate TLS, so SNI routing depends on gateway/pod-level. If some nodes still running old certs or kube-proxy conntrack maps to old backends, you can see failures. conntrack + NAT can cause sessions to stick to drained pods.

kate: can you paste the svc + gateway listener snippet? small snippets help.

anil: sure — here's the relevant bits:

```yaml
# Service (abbreviated)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-grpc
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: "ip"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ports:
    - name: tls
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
```

```yaml
# Gateway listener (abbrev)
spec:
  listeners:
    - name: tls
      protocol: TLS
      port: 443
      tls:
        mode: Passthrough
      hostname: "inference.example.com"
```

infra-bot: deploy-status: gateway/inference-gw rollout started (sha=abc123) at 2287654335.

sre-jen: quick checklist: 1) switch externalTrafficPolicy -> Local; 2) ensure node port healthchecks are reachable from NLB healthcheck IPs; 3) during cert rotation, avoid in-place restart of all pods for same listener — use canary rollout so some pods keep old cert until new cert serves traffic correctly.

kate: also validate kube-proxy conntrack timeouts. Long-lived streams + conntrack entries can map to drained pods until timeout. for grpc streaming we set net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max and related timeouts higher.

anil: good points. one more: when we change target-type from ip -> instance (or vice versa) does it change probe behavior?

sre-jen: yes — target-type=ip makes NLB target pods directly (via ENI IPs), healthchecks hit pod IPs and you must ensure pod ports are open. target-type=instance hits node IP + nodeport which interacts with externalTrafficPolicy. for TLS passthrough we usually prefer ip so TLS goes to pod. but externalTrafficPolicy: Local + ip target requires node IPs for NLB targets to match the node ENI IPs where pods run — more moving parts.

riley: if you want to preserve client src IP for app-level logic, Local + instance with nodePort can work but pod must accept traffic from node. tradeoffs.

anil: ok I'll try: 1) set externalTrafficPolicy: Local 2) confirm target-type stays ip 3) add rolling canary for gateway certs 4) bump conntrack timeout for streams. i'll report back after testing. thanks all :thumbsup:

kate: if you want I can open a tiny terraform/helm PR to flip the svc and add a careful rollout strategy (pre-stop + terminationGracePeriod). ping me when you start the test.

anil: will ping — starting change in staging now (2287654350).

infra-bot: monitor-alert: spike in 502s on inference-grpc between 2287654330-2287654380 — alerted to #incidents.

anil: saw the alert — reverting a recent hotspot config that touched kube-proxy. will update here.

sre-jen: if staging looks good, we can schedule canary on prod with 10% traffic shift and watch error rate for 30m.

anil: noted, thanks everyone.
